ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The title in the figure is “Population Change in the Urban Area of a Certain City from 2001 to 2011”; the left axis is total population, and the right axis is natural growth rate. After 2009, the total population curve continues to rise, increasing roughly from about 4.95 million people in 2009 to about 5.05 million people in 2011; at the same time, the natural growth rate curve declines noticeably, dropping from a relatively high value around 2009 to a relatively low value in 2011. Then reason: The question stem has already excluded the reason “economic development causing relatively large mechanical population growth.” Among the original options, ① “birth rate decreases, and the population of children and adolescents increases” does not fit explaining the total population increase under the background of a declining natural growth rate; ③ “death rate rises, and average life expectancy shortens” generally would make the population decrease, and also cannot explain the total population increase; ② has already been excluded by the question stem. Therefore, the remaining main reason that can lead to an increase in the total urban population is ④ “expansion of college enrollment, increasing the number of students.”
